learningObjective: See why per-request randomization can switch models inside one conversation while per-conversation assignment preserves state.
mediumRationale: A deterministic SVG is the smallest medium that aligns the same ordered turns under two assignment units and makes the mid-conversation model switch spatially obvious. Mermaid adds graph-layout machinery without useful topology; semantic HTML would need article-specific layout rules; interaction adds no lesson beyond the static comparison; reusing a paper figure would add licensing risk and no chatbot-specific sequence; and no visual would leave the article's hardest state-continuity model in prose.

pages.insight: The deck's ML system-design sequence ends with offline and online experimentation tied to a concrete product hypothesis.
The project setup slide explicitly calls generative and dialogue-system evaluation difficult and emphasizes user reactions as imperfect inference-time signals.

deckReview.notes: Reviewed all 214 pages and inspected the exact neighboring sequence on PDF pages 163-166. Page 163 covers requirements and data signals, page 164 covers online experimentation, page 165 covers dialogue-system evaluation, and page 166 begins the data-pipeline section. Pages 164-165 provide relevant context, but none of these pages shows request-, conversation-, or user-level assignment, so no deck figure applies or is reused.

sourceReview.notes: Neither source offers a chatbot-turn figure that is necessary for this lesson. Reuse permission was not assumed from public access; the visual is an original sequence using invented turns and model labels.

agentReview.summary: The hardest mental model is that a request is not an independent exposure when later turns depend on earlier responses. The selected visual contrasts identical turn order under per-request and per-conversation assignment, using labels, borders, line patterns, and position rather than color alone.

implementation.accessibility: The responsive SVG has a title and full prose description. Every turn and model is text-labelled; the problematic switch uses a dashed boundary and warning label, so meaning does not depend on color. Existing learning-figure and plot-panel primitives provide theme tokens, mobile scaling at 390 CSS pixels, and print overrides.
